profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC12 data center at 44790 Performance Circle, Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's cluster of buildings across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC12 facility page publishes building specific numbers rather than only marketing language: 114,323 square feet (10,621 square meters) inside a two story building with a concrete and steel frame and a glass facade. The page lists N+1 redundancy for both the UPS and generator systems, with generators rated to run 30 hours or more at full load, 240v/415v power distribution, and a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA. Cooling redundancy is also listed as N+1, floor load capacity as 250 pounds per square foot, and fire suppression as double interlock pre-action. Equinix lists nine certifications for DC12, HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, and HECVAT, along with a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment and 24/7 biometric mantrap security. The DC12 page also lists sustainability features specific to this building, including wind renewable energy certificates, free cooling, LED lighting, hot and cold aisle containment, solar photovoltaic generation, and grey water reuse. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC12 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley predates Equinix. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project attracted into Loudoun County helped seed the interconnected cluster that followed, including Virginia's early MAE East internet exchange. Equinix opened its first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Data Center Dynamics describes the resulting corridor as roughly 10 million square feet of built data center space region wide, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators combined, not Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group, and at least one building number appearing in public address records for the area, DC17, has no active linked page on Equinix's own site at present. Equinix markets its Ashburn buildings collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, along with Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products, without singling out DC12's own peering density or customer roster.

reading.body:
Equinix DC12 is a 114,323 square foot building in Ashburn, Virginia with N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, and dual-redundant generators rated for 30+ hour runtime. Equinix does not publish megawatt figures for DC12, so the building's IT load cannot be determined from operator specifications. The facility holds nine certifications including HIPAA, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, and PCI DSS, qualifying it to host healthcare, government, and payments workloads.

DC12 sits within Equinix's 15-facility Ashburn campus spanning Loudoun County, which Equinix markets collectively without breaking out individual building densities or customer lists. Data Center Alley is described as the world's largest concentration of data center space at roughly 10 million square feet across all operators, drawing 1 gigawatt of power region-wide. Ashburn hosts one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast and anchors Equinix's interconnection products.

Virginia hosts 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 25 publish power capacity. Equinix DC12 cannot be ranked by published megawatts because no figure is disclosed. The broader Equinix Ashburn campus is ranked 26th in Virginia by published megawatts among facilities with disclosed capacity, but Equinix does not report combined campus figures or per-building allocations for DC12.
